checked_claims.note: Hbar^bal is smooth of pure dimension 15 by CLM-0112-7, and an etale morphism from a connected component of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas is smooth of the same dimension, hence regular, hence normal; a connected normal scheme is integral. The PGL_2-torsor V_tilde=V x_{Hbar^bal} H^bal is connected because PGL_2 is geometrically connected, and V_tilde->H^bal is etale onto a nonempty open of dimension 18, so CLM-0112-6 supplies a type-(i) fibre. FND-0155 plus CLM-0112-8 give monodromy image S_6 on the pulled-back ordering torsor; the image over U contains every base-changed image, so the image over U is already S_6. FND-0151 then makes Z->U connected of degree 720 (full-image criterion, not transitivity on six letters). Grauert on the reduced base with fibrewise h^0(L)=3 (FND-0139, FND-0142) makes A a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle of pure dimension 17; U is a dense open in every fibre by FND-0134, hence pure dimension 17, and Z is finite etale over U. Finite etale over normal U is normal, so connected Z is irreducible. The curve family and residual L descend from V_tilde to V because PGL_2 acts on the target P^1, not on C.

Z->U is a finite etale right S_6-torsor and Z^(1)=Z/S_5, so with Q-coefficients averaging is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures and Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z)^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U), Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z)^{S_5}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1)). Frobenius reciprocity and Ind_{S_5}^{S_6}(1)=[6] direct-sum [5,1] identify the S_5-invariants with the multiplicity spaces M_[6] direct-sum M_[5,1], not with the full isotypic subobjects V_rho tensor M_rho. This uses FND-0152/FND-0166 transfer for free finite etale quotients and does not create Tate type (FND-0053 respected).

FND-0165 applied to the open immersions U subset A and Z^(1) subset D_univ of separated finite-type C-schemes gives injections Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U)->Gr^W_16 H_c^16(A) and Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1))->Gr^W_16 H_c^16(D_univ), because compact-support localization is H_c^{15}(Y)->H_c^{16}(open)->H_c^{16}(total) and Deligne bounds weights on H_c^{15}(Y) by 15. These are not isomorphisms of the ungraded groups. A=P_V(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle, so Rf_!Q=Rf_*Q=Q direct-sum Q(-1)[-2] direct-sum Q(-2)[-4] as constant Tate objects even though V is not proper, and Gr^W_16 of H_c^{16}(A) is the displayed three-term sum. Base-point-freeness (FND-0130, FND-0134) gives h^0(L_s(-p))=2, so D_univ=P_{C_univ}(G) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle and the P^1-bundle formula supplies the two-term target on C_univ. Coefficient objects are constant Tate, the explicit exception in FND-0164; no nonconstant Leray sequence is used. All Hodge groups are on schemes V, A, U, Z, C_univ, D_univ, inside FND-0165's scheme scope, not on the stack Hbar^bal.

Under (H-S), the three summands are Q(-8), Q(-7)(-1)=Q(-8), and Q(-6)(-2)=Q(-8). Under (H-C) both summands of the second injection are Q(-8). Polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of one weight are semisimple, so a subobject of a sum of Q(-8) is a sum of Q(-8): an honest Hodge-structure isomorphism, not a semisimplification (FND-0033). Duality Gr^W_16 H_c^{16} dual to T_16=W_{-16}H_{16}^{BM} in the same degree, with no extra Poincare twist, sends Q(-8) to Q(8). Over Q, invariants equal coinvariants and S_n-irreps are self-dual of type (0,0), so T_16(Z)^{S_6}=T_16(U) and Tate type of the multiplicity spaces M_[6], M_[5,1] yields Tate type of the full [6] and [5,1] isotypic components. Neither hypothesis is asserted; remaining S_6-isotypics, Gysin into M_{6,6}, support exhaustion, stack inertia, integral coefficients, and coarse-moduli descent are correctly disclaimed.

finding_candidates.statement: On every connected component V of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2], compact-support localization plus the constant-Tate P^2 and P^1 projective-bundle formulas inject the weight-16 S_6- and S_5-invariant corners of the ordered reduced-support model into the displayed constant-coefficient corners of V and of the universal curve. Conditional on (H-S) (resp. (H-C)), T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6} (resp. the [6] and [5,1] isotypic components of T_16(Z)) is a sum of Q(8). The argument does not identify discriminant-complement cohomology with projective-bundle cohomology, does not run nonconstant-coefficient Leray, and asserts neither (H-S) nor (H-C) nor any Gysin or support statement on M_{6,6}.

Full S_6 ordering monodromy, and therefore connectedness and irreducibility of the degree-720 right torsor Z->U, is automatic on every connected 15-dimensional etale scheme atlas chart of the PGL_2-quotient stack Hbar^bal. The comparison with the fixed-target stack H^bal is the connected PGL_2-torsor pullback V_tilde=V x_{Hbar^bal} H^bal, which is etale onto a nonempty open of dimension 18 and therefore meets type (i); monodromy over U contains the image after that base change.

theorem_statement: Theorem (balanced-quotient atlas corner lemma). Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2], and let V be a connected component of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal. Pull back the universal balanced tetragonal (CE)+(N) family pi:C_univ->V and its degree-six residual line bundle L. Put A=P_V(pi_*L), let U be the distinct-support open, let Z=Ord(U)->U be the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings, let D_univ be the universal divisor in C_univ x_V A, and put Z^(1)=D_univ x_A U=Z/S_5. Then: (1) V is smooth, normal and integral of dimension 15; A, U and Z have pure dimension 17. The ordering monodromy over U is S_6, so Z->U is connected of degree 720 and Z is irreducible. (2) Writing E=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q), there are canonical injections of pure weight-sixteen Hodge structures E^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q) -> Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(V;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^12(V;Q)(-2), and E^{S_5}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1);Q) -> Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C_univ;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(C_univ;Q)(-1). If E=direct-sum_rho V_rho tensor M_rho is its rational S_6-isotypic decomposition, then E^{S_5}=M_[6] direct-sum M_[5,1]. (3) Consequently, hypothesis (H-S), that Gr^W_{2j}H_c^{2j}(V;Q) is a sum of Q(-j) for j=6,7,8, implies T_16(Z)^{S_6}=T_16(U) is a sum of Q(8); hypothesis (H-C), that Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C_univ;Q) is a sum of Q(-8) and Gr^W_14 H_c^14(C_univ;Q) is a sum of Q(-7), implies that the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic components of T_16(Z)=W_{-16}H_16^{BM}(Z;Q) are sums of Q(8). Neither (H-S) nor (H-C) is asserted here.
